newsitem.title: USA: Democrats demand vote on mortgage insurance bill.
newsitem.headline: Democrats demand vote on mortgage insurance bill.

text.p: Democratic lawmakers Thursday called for a quick vote on a measure to curtail unneccessary mortgage insurance policies that they said cost consumers millions of dollars a year.
"It is outrageous when the Republican leadership cancels a bill with nearly unanimous bipartisan support," Texas Rep. Henry Gonzalez said at a press conference here.

The House of Representatives had scheduled a vote on the bill, H.R. 607 known as the Homeowners Insurance Protection Act, for April 8, but the vote was postponed and has not be rescheduled yet, congressional staffers said Thursday.

Democrats charge that the vote was postponed at the behest of a few mortgage insurance companies. "It's a quintessential demonstration of the power of big business politics," Massachusetts Rep. Joe Kennedy said.
Passed by the House Banking Committee on a 36-to-one vote last month, the bill would allow homeowners to cancel mortgage insurance when they build up sufficient equity.

Currently, mortgage lenders require a borrower to obtain and pay for such insurance when the borrower is making a relatively small down payment, such as five percent of the purchase price of a home. Borrowers putting down 20 percent or more generally are not required to obtain insurance, which can cost $300 to $900 a year.

The bill would automatically cancel a mortgage insurance policy if the homewoner was current on mortgage payments and had built up 25 percent equity of the original value of the house. Homeowner's equity is the value of the home after subtracting the remaining amount of principal on the mortgage.
The bill would not not apply to existing mortgages. The new rules would cover only mortgages and refinancing closed a year after enactment.
Democrats also used the occasion to criticize the overall leadership of Republicans in the House. "This place is in a state of confusion," Rep. Maurice Hinchey of New York said.
Republican leadership offices did not comment earlier in the day on the postponement of the vote.

Both Democrats and Republicans voted for the measure in the House Banking Committee. Committee chairman Jim Leach of Iowa and Gonzalez, ranking Democrat on the panel, have both expressed support for the measure.
Consumer advocates also urged the House to schedule a vote.
"It's really important that we not lose the momentum," Michelle Meier, counsel for government affairs at Consumers Union, said. "It would end an obviously unfair situation for homeowners."
Meier forecast the House would vote on the bill sometime next week.
"I'm still optimistic that this is going to move forward," she said.
If the House passed the bill, focus would turn to the Senate where the Banking Committee has not yet voted on its version of the legislation.
Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato, Republican of New York, has expressed strong support for the measure, but a committee session to amend and vote on a bill was postponed.
